title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from p.117. K is a base field (characteristic 0 in the situation at hand). L/K is a finitely generated field extension of transcendence degree n, with algebraic closure \bar L. E_L = Gal(\bar L/L) is the absolute Galois group, and \pi_{L/K} is the geometric part Gal(\bar L/L\bar K). Let x be a divisorial point: a discrete valuation ring V of L, the local ring of a prime divisor on some model U ⊂ X. Then S_x = Spec V, its henselization is \tilde S_x = Spec \tilde V, and \tilde U_x = Spec \tilde L_x is the generic point of \tilde S_x.

The page makes the 'choice' behind the outer homomorphism E_{\tilde U_x} → E_L precise. Fixing a geometric point of \tilde U_x (an algebraic closure of \tilde L_x) and a 'dictionary' with the fibre functor of L defined by \bar L amounts to the following. Up to isomorphism of extensions, one gives an L-embedding \tilde L_x ↪ \bar L. That in turn is the same as choosing a point x' above x in the normalization of S_x in \bar L. This is the standard correspondence between embeddings of the henselization and prolongations of the valuation.

With this choice, (30) gives the canonical isomorphisms of henselian ('traits henséliens') theory:
- N_{x'} ≅ E^{\bar L}_{\tilde U_x} = Gal(\bar L/\tilde L_x), i.e. the decomposition group is the absolute Galois group of the henselization.
- I_{x'} ≅ Ker(E_{\tilde U_x} → E_{\overline{k(x)}}), where the algebraic closure of the residue field k(x) is the one induced by \bar L.
- In residue characteristic 0 this kernel is \pi_1 of \tilde U_x relative to \tilde S_x (the tame part, via Abhyankar). It is described by Kummer theory as \hat Z(1) = T(\bar K), matching (27) of the previous page.

In (31), marked with a '?', Grothendieck conjectures two things, over a base K of characteristic 0 (or K = C):
- N_{x'} = Norm_{E_L}(I_{x'}): the decomposition group of a divisorial valuation is the normalizer of its inertia group in the absolute Galois group.
- An analogous statement for the normalizer of I_{x'} inside the geometric group \pi_{L/K}.

The next page says 'à tirer au clair'. It then relates I_{x'} → \pi_1(U) to whether the center of the valuation lies in U.
errors: The marginal '(surjectif)' attached to N_{x'} ≅ E_{\tilde U_x} is misleading: the decomposition group is isomorphic to Gal of the henselization. The surjective map is E_{\tilde U_x} → E_{\overline{k(x)}}, the residue field Galois group.

The second part of (31), as transcribed ('I_{x'} = Norm_{\pi_{L/K}}(I_{x'})'), is false for n ≥ 2. Inside the geometric group the normalizer should be N_{x'} ∩ \pi_{L/K}. That maps onto the geometric Galois group of the residue function field k(x), which has transcendence degree n-1 and so is nontrivial. It is correct only for n = 1, the self-normalizing cusp inertia of curves. Most likely the reading intended N_{x'} ∩ \pi_{L/K}, or the line is garbled.
Notation slips between \tilde K_x and \tilde L_x for the fraction field of the henselization.

ideas.what: Choice of an embedding of the henselization into \bar L is equivalent to choosing a point x' above x. This makes the outer map E_{\tilde L_x} → E_L an actual map.
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition group = Galois group of henselization; prolongations of valuations

ideas.what: Inertia group = kernel of Gal(henselian field) → Gal(residue field). In residue characteristic 0 it is \hat Z(1) via Kummer theory and Abhyankar's lemma.
ideas.modern_name: Tame inertia of a discretely valued henselian field
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Abhyankar; SGA1 Exp. XIII (Grothendieck–Murre tame fundamental group)

ideas.what: Conjecture that the decomposition group of a divisorial valuation is the normalizer of its inertia group in the absolute Galois group of a function field.
ideas.modern_name: Self-normalizing / malnormal properties of divisorial inertia; group-theoretic characterization of decomposition groups in birational anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Neukirch (number field analogue, 1969); Pop, Bogomolov–Tschinkel, Engler–Koenigsmann (function fields, 1990s–2000s)
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme / letter to Faltings (birational anabelian program), but not this exact statement as far as I know

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly poses, as an open question to 'clarify', that divisorial decomposition groups are normalizers of divisorial inertia in G_L. This is an early local-theory step of the birational anabelian program.
missed.quote: Je présume que ... on a N_{x'} = Norm_{\mathcal E_L}(I_{x'})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that Grothendieck was thinking about the group-theoretic recognition of divisorial inertia and decomposition groups. That 'local theory' was later developed by Pop and Bogomolov–Tschinkel. The statement itself is now essentially known, so this is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly standard henselian ramification theory. The conjecture N = Norm(I) anticipates known results of birational anabelian geometry (Neukirch-type characterizations, Pop's local theory), so it is not a new result. It is a mildly interesting dating of Grothendieck's thoughts on divisorial inertia.
transcription_corrections: 'dico des données' is plausibly 'iso des données' or 'dictionnaire des données'; the sense is an identification of fibre functors.
Margin '(Abhyankar[?] Ref[?])' likely reads '(lemme d'Abhyankar)' or '(Abhyankar)', referring to the tame description via Kummer theory.
'clôture alg[?]/k(x)' should be 'clôture alg. \overline{k(x)} de k(x)'.
The final line is probably not 'I_{x'} = Norm_{\pi_{L/K}}(I_{x'})' as stated; it is likely a normalizer statement inside \pi_{L/K} with some other left-hand side, given the subscript \pi_{L/K}.
